newsitem.title: UK: Norway's DNV to evaluate Shell Brent Spar proposal.
newsitem.headline: Norway's DNV to evaluate Shell Brent Spar proposal.

text.p: Independent advisory body Norway's Det Norske Veritas (DNV) has been commissioned by Shell U.K. Exploration and Production to evaluate proposals for disposal of the controversial Brent Spar loading buoy.
DNV said it had been asked to assess the technical, safety and environmental aspects of 11 shortlisted proposals for re-using or scrapping Brent Spar.
The proposals range from simple scrapping to adapting the rig for use as a fish farm or as part of a coastal defence scheme.

Shell Expro, which operates in the North Sea on behalf of Royal/Dutch Shell Group and Exxon Corp, in January selected six engineering companies to make detailed proposals for a total of 11 plans for the rig.
Brent Spar has been moored in a Norwegian fjord ever since a campaign led by the environmental group Greenpeace in 1995 scuppered its plans to ditch the platform in the Atlantic Ocean.
Shell must persuade the British government that any of the 11 alternatives is better than deep sea disposal.
